Saying: Let your conscience be your guide
WhatItMeans: Your inner voice knows right from wrong, so the safest path through life is simply to follow what your conscience tells you.
WhatTheBibleSays: The Bible does speak of conscience — Romans 2:15 says the conscience bears witness, accusing or else excusing — but it never tells us to follow it as a guide, and for good reason: conscience can be misled. "The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked" (Jeremiah 17:9), and Paul warns of consciences seared with a hot iron (1 Timothy 4:2). A clear conscience did not prove Paul right either — "I know nothing by myself; yet am I not hereby justified" (1 Corinthians 4:4). I hold that conscience is a witness, not a compass: it can tell you something is wrong, but only God's word can tell you what is right.
Origin: Best known from Walt Disney's Pinocchio (1940), where the Blue Fairy tells Pinocchio to "always let your conscience be your guide," and Jiminy Cricket sings it in "Give a Little Whistle." An older origin is sometimes claimed — Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab is said to have used the words in his address at Jabiah after the surrender of Jerusalem (c. 638) — but no primary source verifies the English wording as an accurate translation, so that attribution is reported, not certain.
Sources: Disney, Pinocchio (1940); on-site KJV text of Romans 2:15, Jeremiah 17:9 and 1 Timothy 4:2
